item.title: Jackson Boxer’s vegan recipe for almond sorbet with grape granita
item.description:
【AI 精简版】 AI-condensed version. This text was produced by an LLM from the original article and may omit details. The original link at the end is the only authoritative source. (Refinement was skipped, so the body is an excerpt of the original.)

Ice-cream holds an irresistible allure for me. That combination of richness, lightness, and the pure, sensual pleasure of it melting gently across the palate maintains an unbreakable hold over my imagination. In fact, other than fruit, it’s the only sweet food with which I have a genuine emotional relationship: I can remember many ice-creams I’ve eaten incredibly vividly, and in a way I just don’t with almost all other desserts and pastries. Today’s ice is a case in point, having been developed from a memory of an almond gelato eaten in Sicily just after the annual harvest.

Almond sorbet with grape granita

The amaretto and tonka beans help round out the flavour in a way that old blanched almonds off the shelf might not.

Prep 10 min

Cook 15 min

Chill/freeze 2 hr+

Serves 4

For the sorbet syrup

250g sugar

160g glucose powder

10g xanthan gum

For the sorbet

400g blanched almonds

700

ml almond milk – Plenish is by far the best

100ml amaretto

4 tonka beans (about 5g)

4g flaky sea salt

(about 1 tsp)

500ml sorbet syrup (see above and method)

For the granita

1kg black seedless grapes

125ml light red wine – a vegan beaujolais is ideal

Fresh lemon juice, to taste

First make the syrup. Put everything in a bowl or jug with 120ml water, stir until the sugar and glucose dissolve and the xanthan gum has hydrated, then put in the fridge to chill.

Put all the sorbet ingredients bar the syrup in a blender and blitz on full speed for 10 minutes. Add the sorbet syrup and blend again, this time on low speed, for another minute. Put in the fridge until cold, then transfer to an ice-cream machine and churn (if you don’t have a machine, decant into a suitable container, freeze for 30 minutes, then scrape and beat vigorously with a fork. Return to the freezer, and repeat at half-hourly intervals until you have a smooth ice).

Now for the granita. Pick the grapes off their vines, removing and discarding all stems, then blend on low speed until totally pulped. Pass the grape pulp through a fine sieve, so you’re left with just the juice, then discard the grape solids. Stir in the wine, then add lemon juice to taste – you want to brighten up the flavour and balance the sweetness, so the amount will depend on how sweet the grapes are and on personal taste: I like quite a lot of acidity to temper the sweetness of the fruit.

Transfer the granita mix to a container, cover and put in the freezer. After 20 minutes, remove, use a metal whisk to break up any ice formations and return to the freezer. Repeat every 20 minutes for about two hours, until you have a nice, even, cloud-like snow of granita.

Using an ice-cream scoop or a warm spoon, put two scoops of the sorbet in four very well-chilled bowls (put them in the freezer first), then spread out a little. Top with two spoonfuls of granita, then spread that out evenly, too. Top with another scoop of sorbet and serve at once.

- Jackson Boxer is chef/owner of Brunswick House, Vesper and Dove, all in London, and culinary director of Cowley Manor near Cheltenham and the Henrietta in London

item.description:

For Shuai Wang, chef of King BBQ in North Charleston, South Carolina, mochi brings back memories of holidays with family. His other dessert love? Classic Southern pecan pie. This Hawaiian-style butter mochi cake draws on both, pairing a rich, chewy cake with a generous layer of maple-miso pecans.

The batter gets its signature bounce from mochiko, a distinct style of rice flour that gives butter mochi its chewy texture—not the fluffy crumb of a conventional cake. Coconut milk and melted butter add richness, while the pecans provide crunch. Let the cake cool completely before slicing so the texture has time to set.

The secret to the pecan topping is a little white or yellow miso, which brings savory depth to the maple syrup, much like the salt in salted caramel. The nuts need only a brief head start in the oven; they’ll continue to toast as the cake bakes.

Can I use regular rice flour instead of mochiko?

No. Mochiko, also called sweet or glutinous rice flour, has a different starch composition from regular rice flour. It’s responsible for butter mochi’s characteristic springy, slightly sticky chew. Regular rice flour or all-purpose flour won’t produce the same texture.

What kind of miso is best for baking?

White and yellow miso are both good choices for this cake. White miso tends to be milder and slightly sweeter, while yellow miso has a somewhat more pronounced savory flavor. Either adds complexity to the maple-coated pecans without overwhelming their buttery, nutty flavor. Learn more about the different types of miso and how to use them.

Is butter mochi cake gluten-free?

Mochiko is naturally gluten-free, despite the sometimes confusing name glutinous rice flour. This recipe can be gluten-free, but check your miso: Some varieties contain barley or wheat. If you’re baking for someone who needs to avoid gluten, choose a miso labeled gluten-free and check your other packaged ingredients.

- Rimmed Baking Sheet $35 At Amazon

- Rubber Spatula $13 At Amazon

Preparation

- Pecans Step 1 Place a rack in middle of oven; preheat to 350°. Lightly oil a rimmed baking sheet with vegetable oil. Whisk 2 Tbsp. pure maple syrup and 2 tsp. white or yellow miso (gluten-free if needed) in a medium bowl until smooth. Add 8 oz. raw pecans, coarsely chopped (about 2 cups) and 1 Tbsp. sugar and toss until evenly coated. Spread out on prepared baking sheet; bake until fragrant and matte looking, 6–8 minutes (nuts won’t be fully toasted). Let cool.

- Cake and Assembly Step 2 Lightly grease a 9"-diameter cake pan with unsalted butter and line bottom with a parchment paper round. Vigorously whisk 2 large eggs, 1¼ cups (250 g) sugar, and 1 tsp. Diamond Crystal or ½ tsp. Morton kosher salt in a large bowl until smooth. Add one 13.5-oz. can unsweetened coconut milk, well shaken, heated slightly if fat is solid, 2 tsp. vanilla bean paste or vanilla extract, and 6 Tbsp. unsalted butter, melted, slightly cooled, and whisk well. Add 1⅔ cups (254 g) mochiko and 1 tsp. baking powder; whisk vigorously until combined and batter is smooth and thick. Scrape batter into prepared pan. Step 3 Toss pecans to break up any clumps and scatter evenly over batter, going all the way to the edges (it may seem like a lot). Bake cake until sides start to pull away from pan, top is golden brown, and a tester inserted into the center comes out clean (some pecans will sink), 50–55 minutes. If pecans begin to brown too quickly, loosely tent pan with foil. Transfer to a wire rack and let cake cool in pan 15 minutes. Turn cake out onto rack; peel away parchment and discard. Carefully turn cake right side up and let cool completely (at least 1 hour). Step 4 To serve, slice cake and top with scoops of vanilla ice cream. Do Ahead: Cake can be made 1 day ahead. Store, loosely covered, at room temperature. Editor’s note: This recipe was first published in our August 2023 issue and has been updated with additional guidance. Dirty Spaghetti

Dirty rice has met its noodle match with our Louisiana-style dirty spaghetti.

Let the good times roll with this Louisiana-inspired dirty spaghetti dish! It’s a riff on Cajun-Creole dirty rice that transforms the original into an easy one-pot pasta.

The key it its flavor is Cajun seasoning, a blend cayenne pepper, garlic powder, black pepper, paprika and thyme. And herein lies an important cooking tip: When using store-bought seasoning blends like this one, give them a little taste first before adding anything to the pot. Different brands rely on different ratios of ingredients, and a tablespoon of one product could be much milder (or pack way more heat!) than a tablespoon of another. Your personal preferences matter, too. So whether you are sensitive to spice or like to pack on the heat, make sure you’re adding the proper amount of spice for your taste.

What is dirty spaghetti?

Dirty spaghetti is a riff on dirty rice, a classic Cajun-Creole side dish. Traditional dirty rice is made with chopped organ meats such as chicken livers or gizzards, which, along with the herbs and seasonings, color the white rice and earn it its “dirty” moniker. This dish, however, has a meaty base that’s made with ground beef and diced andouille sausage. Like the original, it also features the “holy trinity” of Cajun and Creole cooking: chopped onion, bell pepper and celery. A healthy dose of Cajun seasoning ensures each bite is packed with bold flavor.

Dirty Spaghetti Ingredients

- Olive oil: A drizzle of olive oil is used to saute the meat and veggies.

- Holy trinity: Chopped yellow onion, green and red bell pepper and celery provide a flavorful base for this dish’s meaty sauce.

- Ground beef: A blend of beef that’s 90% lean retains plenty of flavor and is ideal for this recipe.

- Andouille sausage: This smoked sausage has roots in France, but has become a staple of Louisiana cooking. It has a deeply smoky and spicy flavor, and is traditionally seasoned with Cayenne pepper, garlic, black pepper and thyme.

- Garlic: Use freshly minced garlic for the most robust flavor.

- Tomato paste: Tomato paste adds richness and complexity to the sauce.

- Seasoning: Cajun seasoning is the star of the show here. Be sure to give it a taste before adding it to the recipe to gauge how spicy it is, as different blends can vary widely in terms of heat. After the dish is cooked, season the spaghetti to taste with salt and black pepper.

- Beef broth: Use a low-sodium beef broth to control the salt, because both the Cajun seasoning and sausage add their own saltiness. Of course, store-bought beef broth works perfectly fine here, but homemade beef stock is also a great option.

- Spaghetti: You will need 8 ounces of dry spaghetti for this recipe. (Assume about 2 ounces of spaghetti per person.) To cook the spaghetti without it clumping, break the noodles in half before adding them to the simmering sauce.

Directions

Step 1: Brown the beef

Heat the oil in a large Dutch oven or large high-sided skillet over medium-high heat. Add the ground beef and cook it until it’s browned, four to six minutes, using a wooden spoon or spatula to break it into small crumbles.

Editor’s Tip: If you use a skillet, make sure it has a lid.

Step 2: Add the sausage and veggies

Add the chopped andouille sausage, onion, celery, red pepper and green pepper. Cook them until the vegetables are soft, about three to four minutes. Add the garlic and cook it until it’s fragrant, 30 to 60 seconds. Stir in the tomato paste and Cajun seasoning, and cook for one to two more minutes. Add 3 cups of broth and bring the mixture to a simmer.

Step 3: Add the spaghetti

Add the broken spaghetti to the pot, ensuring that the noodles are submerged in the liquid and separated as much as possible. Add more liquid if needed. Bring the mixture to a boil, then reduce the heat to medium-low. Cover the pot and simmer the pasta for six minutes.

Remove the lid and continue simmering until the spaghetti is al dente, stirring every two to three minutes. Add more broth as needed. Remove the pot from the heat, and season the pasta to taste with salt and pepper.

Dirty Spaghetti Variations

- Lower the heat: For a less-spicy dirty spaghetti, use just a teaspoon of Cajun seasoning. You can also substitute Italian hot sausage, chicken sausage or a mild smoked sausage like kielbasa for the andouille sausage.

- Add a green garnish: Top the spaghetti with sliced green onions or fresh chopped parsley.

How to Store Dirty Spaghetti

Leftover dirty spaghetti can be stored in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to four days.

What is the best way to reheat dirty spaghetti?

The best way to reheat a pasta dish like this one is either in the oven or on the stovetop. To reheat leftover dirty spaghetti in the oven, transfer it to an oven-safe baking dish, cover it tightly with foil, and cook it in an oven preheated to 350 degrees for about 20 minutes or until it’s heated through. To reheat it on the stovetop, heat a saucepan over medium heat and add a drizzle of olive oil. Add the leftover pasta and sauce and saute them for about two to three minutes or until they’re hot.

Can you freeze dirty spaghetti?

Yes, you can freeze dirty spaghetti. After allowing it to cool completely, transfer leftovers to a freezer-safe container and store them in the freezer for up to three months. Allow the dirty spaghetti to thaw overnight in the fridge before reheating it.

Dirty Spaghetti Tips

What’s the best pan for making one-pan dirty spaghetti?

The best pan for making this one-pot pasta dish is a Dutch oven or a large, high-walled skillet or pot with a tight-fitting lid.

How do I make this dirty spaghetti less spicy?

First, be sure to give your Cajun seasoning a little taste first because seasoning blends like this one can vary widely in spiciness. Depending on how spicy your Cajun seasoning is, add more or less to taste. You could also make a homemade Cajun seasoning blend and customize the amount of cayenne pepper and chili powder to your personal taste. The andouille sausage also adds quite a bit of spice; for less heat, skip it entirely, or swap in sweet Italian sausage, breakfast sausage, chicken sausage or a milder smoked sausage like kielbasa.

What should I serve with dirty spaghetti?

You’ll definitely want to pair this dirty spaghetti with crusty French bread, garlic bread or cornbread to sop up any extra sauce. Southern-inspired side dishes to consider include southern green beans, collard greens or black-eyed pea tomato salad. Or, complement the pasta dish’s spicy flavor with a fresh and crisp green salad.

Source: Taste of Home | Published: 2026-11-20 16:03 UTC

Slashing bone-in chicken thighs (carefully, around the bone, of course) allows a punchy maple-Dijon-ACV marinade to permeate the meat deeply in a short amount of time. And that waiting time is well spent: Scatter torn sourdough bread on a baking sheet and bake until crisp, then toss croutons aside to make way for the thighs. Once the chicken is cooked through, toss the croutons in the rendered fat and cook until everything is bronzed and glistening. A few handfuls of arugula make an elegant finish—who needs a side salad?

Recipe information

- Total Time 1 hour 10 minutes

- Yield 4 servings

Ingredients

5

½

8

3

1

2½

1

3

2

Need to make a substitution?

Preparation

- Step 1 Whisk 5 garlic cloves, finely grated, ½ cup plus 3 Tbsp. apple cider vinegar, 5 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil, 3 Tbsp. Dijon mustard, 1 Tbsp. plus 2 tsp. pure maple syrup, 2½ tsp. Diamond Crystal or 1½ tsp. Morton kosher salt, and 1 tsp. crushed red pepper flakes (if using) in a measuring glass or small bowl to combine. Transfer 2 Tbsp. vinegar mixture to a small bowl; set aside. Step 2 Arrange 3 lb. skin-on, bone-in chicken thighs (6–8), skin side up, on a cutting board. Season lightly with salt. Turn over and season lightly on other side with salt, then carefully use a sharp paring knife to make 3 long slashes, going most of the way through meat (avoid the bone). Transfer to a large bowl and pour vinegar mixture in measuring glass over. Toss chicken to coat, making sure to get liquid into slashes. Let chicken sit at least 30 minutes and up to 1 hour. Step 3 Meanwhile, place a rack in middle of oven; preheat to 425°. Place 8 oz. country-style or sourdough bread (about ⅓ loaf), torn into 1" pieces, on a rimmed baking sheet. Drizzle remaining 3 Tbsp. extra-virgin olive oil over and sprinkle with a pinch of salt and a pinch of freshly ground black pepper; toss to coat. Arrange bread in a single layer and bake until golden, 12–15 minutes. Transfer croutons to a plate; reserve baking sheet. Step 4 Arrange reserved chicken on reserved baking sheet and nestle 3 large shallots, quartered lengthwise through root ends, around; pour any excess vinegar mixture in bowl over. Bake chicken until golden, cooked through, and an instant-read thermometer inserted into thickest part, avoiding bone, registers at least 165° (it should be well over), 25–30 minutes. Step 5 Scatter croutons over empty areas of baking sheet and toss to soak up juices. Roast until chicken and croutons are deeply browned, 10–12 minutes. Let cool 5 minutes, then top with 2 oz. arugula and drizzle with reserved vinegar mixture in small bowl.
